newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open softer amid U.S. weakness.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open softer amid U.S. weakness.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened weaker in quiet trade on Monday, softening with their U.S. counterparts as both markets remained focused on Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve, dealers said.

"The U.S. is weaker and people are trying to square up positions," said one Toronto T-bill trader. "Nobody is going to stand in and offer a lot of support today on either side of the market. I wouldn't be surprised to see it jump around because the volume is probably going to be a little bit thin."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.96 percent from 3.95 percent on Friday.
The Fed's rate-setting Open Market Committee meets tomorrow and dealers said the market remained almost evenly divided on the possibility that the central bank would hike U.S. interest rates.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued bill softened to yield 4.26 percent from 4.24 percent at Friday's close. The one-year when-issued bill weakened to yield 4.71 percent from 4.68 percent.
Dealers said the call loan or overnight lending rate was trading at 4.0 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 3.75-4.25 percent target range.
